title: Anatomy of a Fan Duty Statement
description: The learner clicks the six parts of an illustrative fan duty statement (12,000 CFM at 3.0 in. wg static pressure, 1,173 RPM, 7.9 BHP, at 0.075 lb/ft³, clean air) to read what each tells, then names each highlighted part in a shuffled one-attempt quiz.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: Duty statement
Airflow volume
Static pressure
Fan speed
Brake horsepower
Air density
Airstream
rights: Copyright 2026 Twin City Fan. All rights reserved.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: The six parts of a fan duty statement
learningObjectives: The learner will identify each of the six parts of a fan duty statement by its quantity and unit, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Airflow volume and cubic feet per minute
Static pressure and inches of water gauge

accessibility.notes: Segments are focusable buttons (role=button) with aria-labels; quiz hides the names from screen readers until revealed; verdicts and prompts announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗/→ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; keys 1-6 pick a name; focus moves to Next prompt after an answer.

controls.label: Explore
controls.purpose: Explore mode: click segments to open their callouts

controls.label: Duty statement parts
controls.purpose: Six clickable segments of the rating line (Enter or Space)

controls.label: 1-6 quantity names
controls.purpose: Choose the name of the highlighted segment (keys 1-6)

controls.label: Start over / Back to explore
controls.purpose: New quiz, or return to Explore mode, from the summary

simulation.modelType: Labeled infographic with a matching quiz
rules: Each segment has exactly one correct quantity name; each name is used once
Quiz order shuffled with a seed chosen once per session
One scored attempt per segment; the answer is revealed after it
Mastery: 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt
limitations: The duty statement combines values from two worked examples and is illustrative, not a catalog selection

sources: Chapter 1 worked examples 'From Duty Point to Motor' (12,000 CFM, 3.0 in. wg, 7.9 BHP, 10 hp, 79 percent) and 'Setting a Belt-Driven Fan's Speed' (1,760 RPM, 6 in and 9 in sheaves, 1,173 RPM)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labeled parts with callouts, then retrieve the names without support
keyQuestions: What does each number in a duty statement tell you?
Why can a duty statement without a density or an airstream not be checked against a catalog?
commonMisconceptions: BHP is the motor nameplate size.
The static pressure is a property of the fan alone rather than the resistance of the system at that airflow.
The density can be left off because every catalog uses standard air.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'Correct on first attempt: n of 6'; mastery is 5 of 6 on the first attempt.
Explore mode is not evidence of mastery
